SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Cloudflare, Inc. (NET) on Thursday reported a loss of $34.1 million in its third quarter.

The San Francisco-based company said it had a loss of 10 cents per share. Earnings, adjusted for one-time gains and costs, came to 38 cents per share.

The results topped Wall Street expectations. The average estimate of 10 analysts surveyed by Zacks Investment Research was for earnings of 35 cents per share.

The web security and content delivery company posted revenue of $782.5 million in the period, also topping Street forecasts. Ten analysts surveyed by Zacks expected $734.3 million.

For the current quarter ending in December, Cloudflare expects its per-share earnings to be 43 cents.

The company said it expects revenue in the range of $845 million to $846 million for the fiscal fourth quarter.

Cloudflare expects full-year earnings to be $1.35 per share, with revenue expected to be $2.96 billion.

Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) delivers strong Q3 2026 numbers, stock jumps 18.2%

Cloud security and performance company Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) reported revenue ahead of Wall Street's expectations in Q3 2026, with revenue up 39.2% year on year to $782.5 million. In addition, next quarter's revenue guidance ($845.5 million at the midpoint) was surprisingly strong, at 6.2% above analysts' consensus estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.38 per share was 10.6% above analysts' consensus estimates.

For more on Cloudflare, read our full research report.

Cloudflare (NET) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $782.5 million vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $736.8 million (39.2% year-on-year growth, 6.2% beat)

Adjusted EPS $0.38 vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $0.34 (10.6% beat)

Adjusted operating income $137.1 million vs analysts' consensus estimates of $129.7 million (17.5% margin, 5.7% beat)

Revenue guidance $845.5 million at the midpoint for Q4 2026, above analysts' consensus estimates of $795.9 million

Adjusted EPS guidance Management raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.35 at the midpoint, a 7.6% increase

Operating margin -8.7%, down from -6.7% in the same quarter last year

Free cash flow margin 10.5%, up from 8.1% in the previous quarter

Billings $846.2 million at quarter end, up 35.5% year on year

Market capitalization $94.92 billion

Revenue growth

A company's long-term performance is an indicator of its overall quality. Any business can deliver a good quarter or two, but many enduring ones grow for years. Cloudflare's 35.9% annualized revenue growth over the last five years was strong. Its growth surpassed the average software company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.

Cloudflare quarterly revenue

Long-term growth is the most important, but within software, a half-decade historical view may miss new innovations or demand cycles. Cloudflare's annualized revenue growth of 31.8% over the last two years is below its five-year trend, but the results still suggest healthy demand.

Cloudflare year-on-year revenue growth

This quarter, Cloudflare reported year-on-year revenue growth of 39.2%, and its $782.5 million of revenue exceeded Wall Street's consensus estimates by 6.2%. Management is guiding for a 37.6% year-on-year increase in revenue next quarter.

Looking further ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 26.9% over the next 12 months, according to S&P, a deceleration versus the last two years. Despite the slowdown, this projection is healthy and indicates the market expects continued success for its products and services.

Billings

Billings is a non-GAAP metric that is often called "cash revenue" because it shows how much money the company has collected from customers in a certain period. This is different from revenue, which must be recognized in pieces over the length of a contract.

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare fell 8% today, ahead of its third-quarter report, as the AI selloff that followed Democrats' sweep of Congress spread to software stocks.

The campaign took aim at AI data centers, and Cloudflare's business doesn't depend much on them directly.

Cloudflare guided for 31% revenue growth this quarter and has beaten the top of its guidance in each of the last three.

The stock still trades at a steep multiple, so tonight's numbers have to hold up.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) sank 8% today, ahead of its third-quarter report, as the AI selloff that hammered chip stocks spread to software.

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress after a campaign in which candidates from both parties took aim at AI data centers.

As Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre put it, "The stocks that had the best year are now the ones with the most to lose." Cloudflare had climbed sharply in 2026, and it's on pace for its worst day since May.

Congress is the wrong worry here

Cloudflare's tie to AI data centers is mostly indirect. CEO Matthew Prince's rule is to "invest behind demand," adding servers to its network after customers show up. And its CFO said last year that no AI-native customer made up more than 2% of revenue.

Okta (OKTA:NASDAQ), down 11% with no news of its own, shows the whole group is getting sold. It guided for 10% revenue growth this quarter, a third of Cloudflare's pace, and fell just as hard. When it reports in a few weeks, watch whether its current remaining performance obligations grow the 11%-12% it guided for.

Cloudflare needs another big beat

Cloudflare guided for third-quarter revenue of $736 million to $737 million, and it has beaten the top of its range by 3% to 5% in each of the last three quarters. Analysts expect growth near 30% a year through 2028:

Cloudflare's non-GAAP gross margin was 73.1% in the second quarter, down from 76.3% a year earlier, as its fast-growing developer products carry lower margins. The last time the stock fell this hard, in May, it dropped about 24% after reporting a first-quarter gross margin of 72.8%.

There's little room for a miss at this price. Cloudflare traded at 179x forward earnings at Monday's close, above its 173x quarter-end average since mid-2023. After today's drop, it sits near that average, which is still a lot to pay.

title: Cloudflare Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
detail:
This is a paid press release. Contact the press release distributor directly with any inquiries.
Cloudflare Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
Business Wire
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:15 PM PST 27 min read
NET
Trade NET on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Third quarter revenue totaled $782.5 million, representing an increase of 39% year-over-year

GAAP loss from operations of $67.9 million, or 9% of total revenue, and non-GAAP income from operations of $137.1 million, or 18% of revenue

Delivered Current RPO year-over-year growth of 37%

SAN FRANCISCO, November 05, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET), the leading connectivity cloud company, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

"The third quarter was Cloudflare's best quarter ever. We crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue with revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year. We accelerated growth, delivering our fastest revenue growth in nearly four years, while expanding profitability," said Matthew Prince, co-founder & CEO of Cloudflare. "We have built the development platform for the AI-powered Internet—and as digital threats escalate, organizations of every size continue to rely on Cloudflare for protection. Our engine is firing on all cylinders, and we've found an even higher gear for this next phase of growth."

Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Highlights

Revenue: Total revenue of $782.5 million, representing an increase of 39% year-over-year.

Gross Profit: GAAP gross profit was $557.2 million, or 71.2% gross margin, compared to $415.7 million, or 74.0%, in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP gross profit was $566.6 million, or 72.4% gross margin, compared to $423.1 million, or 75.3%, in the third quarter of 2025.

Operating Income (Loss): GAAP loss from operations was $67.9 million, or 8.7% of revenue, compared to $37.5 million, or 6.7% of revenue, in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP income from operations was $137.1 million, or 17.5% of revenue, compared to $85.9 million, or 15.3% of revenue, in the third quarter of 2025.

Net Income (Loss): GAAP net loss was $34.1 million, compared to $1.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. GAAP net loss per basic and diluted share was $0.10, compared to $0.00 in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP net income was $143.7 million, compared to $102.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP net income per diluted share was $0.38, compared to $0.27 in the third quarter of 2025.

Cash Flow: Net cash flow from operating activities was $215.4 million, compared to $167.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. Free cash flow was $82.1 million, or 10% of revenue, compared to $75.0 million, or 13% of revenue, in the third quarter of 2025.

Cash, cash equivalents, and available-for-sale securities were $5,128.7 million as of September 30, 2026.

Key Takeaways

CrowdStrike shares fell 10% as investors sold off AI stocks, and the company had no news to explain the drop.

Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and Cloudflare fell with it, as the market sold cybersecurity as a group.

CrowdStrike's forward P/E sits far above its five-year average, while earnings estimates have barely risen.

Its Dec. 1 report has to show that AI-driven demand is lasting.

CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) sank 10% today with no news of its own, as the Nasdaq-100 fell 5% and investors unwound the AI trade. Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ), Zscaler (ZS:NASDAQ) and Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) sold off with it.

It's a rough end to a good week for CrowdStrike's business. On Tuesday, it launched a kill switch for rogue AI agents and agreed to buy two AI-agent security startups, Fiddler and Dreadnode, for about $495 million combined, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Analysts barely raised their numbers

Analysts expect revenue to grow 25% to $6.01 billion in the year ending January 2027, then about 22% to 23% a year after that.

CrowdStrike (CRWD): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (years to January) (TIKR)

Nothing in today's drop should move those estimates. But they've barely moved all year: consensus EPS for each of the next three fiscal years is up 5% at most over the past year, while the stock ripped 114% in 2026 through Monday.

So investors are paying a lot more for the same earnings. CrowdStrike traded at 171x forward earnings at Wednesday's close, against a five-year average of 113x.

CrowdStrike (CRWD): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

At today's price, it's about 156x.

The demand is real: net new ARR jumped 51% to a record $332.8 million in the quarter ended July 31.

title: 5 Things Investors Need to Know About Thursday’s Markets

Stocks rocked higher in post-election trading Wednesday.
Credit: Michael Nagle / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Stock futures are pointing toward a mixed opening on Thursday, with futures tied to the S&P 500 faintly higher and those associated with Nasdaq 100 looking downward; the Dow looks like it could extend recent gains; Toyota shares are rising after the automaker lifted its outlook; AppLovin and Dutch Bros' shares are making relatively big moves, albeit in opposite directions; and investors are preparing for quarterly results from Airbnb and Cloudflare.

Here's what you need to know today.

Stock Futures Look Mixed

Stock futures looked mixed ahead of the opening bell after yesterday's big, and broad, post-election rally. Futures tied to the Dow were up about 0.7%, those tied to the S&P 500 were up 0.1%, and those associated with the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 were down some 0.8%.

Oil prices were rising, with Brent crude—the global oil benchmark—up about 3% to almost $98 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate—the U.S. benchmark—up some 2.5% to near $90 a barrel. The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury notes was close to 4.89%, where it stood last night. The price of precious metals was increasing, as was bitcoin, which was recently trading for more than $79,600, according to CoinDesk.

Read today's full markets roundup here.

Dow Looks Poised for More Gains

The Dow appeared poised to climb again, with futures tied to the blue-chip index pointing higher. The Dow jumped 1,569 points, or 3%, on Wednesday, marking the index's fifth-largest one-day increase. All but three companies in the index logged gains yesterday with members like 3M (MMM), Microsoft (MSFT), Sherwin-Williams (SHW), McDonald's (MCD), Home Depot (HD) and Amazon (AMZN) all rising more than 5%. Tech isn't as widely represented in the Dow as in some other indexes, which may be making the Dow more attractive to investors who want to reduce their exposure to AI.

Toyota Shares Take Off on Brighter Outlook

A big Japanese carmaker's shares are driving higher this morning. Toyota's (TM) stock was recently up some 9% in U.S. trading as the company reported falling profits, but lifted its full-year outlook. (They rose more than 16% in Japan.) Toyota's latest quarterly net income fell nearly 19% year-over-year to 759.4 billion yen as the manufacturer grappled with rising supply costs and U.S. tariffs, according to the company. Still, Toyota now expects 3.57 trillion yen in profit, up from 3.25 trillion yen in prior estimates.

AppLovin, Dutch Bros' Shares Are Big Morning Movers

Digital advertising company AppLovin (APP) and coffee chain Dutch Bros (BROS) were among the morning's biggest premarket movers. AppLovin shares were recently up some 22% after the company reported a 72% year-over-year jump in profit and record revenue on Wednesday. Dutch Bros' shares were off more than 11% after the drive-thru chain published a muted forecast with its quarterly results on Wednesday. Dutch Bros' full-year forecast of "at least $2.1 billion" matched the $2.13 billion expected, according to Visible Alpha's survey of analysts. Slower sales may have investors worried about inflation-weary consumers cutting back—a concern that has dogged rivals like Starbucks and other quick-service restaurants.
